summary: A Tibetan font that pairs Tibetan script with a slanted, calligraphic Latin. Used for writing Tibetan, Dzongkha and related languages on the Mac.
history: Developed by Prof. Shojiro Nomura of Otani University's Shin Buddhist research institute in Kyoto with Steve Hartwell. Apple added it, along with Kailasa, when Mac OS X 10.5 Leopard brought built-in Unicode Tibetan support.
designers: Shojiro Nomura and Steve Hartwell (Otani University)

links.label: Digital Tibetan: macOS and Tibetan script

summary: A heavy, blocky Thai display font whose Latin letters are the same as Apple's classic Chicago system font. Best for headings and short bold text.
history: An Apple Thai font with a file copyright going back to 1992. It is one of the Thai fonts Apple has long shipped with its Mac systems, and it shares its name with Krung Thep, the Thai name for Bangkok.

summary: A bold Arabic font in a geometric, Kufi-inspired style, with angular shapes and a strong horizontal line. Works well for headings and signage-like text.
history: Designed by Diwan Software, a company that worked with Apple on Arabic fonts for the Arabic Macintosh in the 1990s. Its file copyright runs from 1992 to 1998, and it has shipped with macOS for many years.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A Lao font for the Lao language, whose Latin letters use a humanist sans with noticeable stroke contrast (the shared "MN" Latin design). Suited to reading text on the Mac.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts bundled with Apple's operating systems. It is one of the "MN" families that ship with macOS.

summary: A Lao font from Apple's "Sangam MN" series, pairing Lao letterforms with a plain grotesque-style sans serif for Latin. Good for the Lao language text in apps and on screen.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts for Apple. The Sangam MN families are a sans-style counterpart to the MN fonts and ship with macOS.

summary: A Malayalam font for the Malayalam language of Kerala, whose Latin letters use a humanist sans with noticeable stroke contrast (the shared "MN" Latin design). Suited to reading text on the Mac.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts bundled with Apple's operating systems. It is one of the "MN" families that ship with macOS.

summary: A Malayalam font from Apple's "Sangam MN" series, pairing Malayalam letterforms with a plain grotesque-style sans serif for Latin. Good for the Malayalam language of Kerala text in apps and on screen.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts for Apple. The Sangam MN families are a sans-style counterpart to the MN fonts and ship with macOS.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A formal Arabic font in a Naskh-style calligraphic hand, made for setting the Quran, Hadith and classical poetry. Graceful and ornate, best for religious and literary texts rather than UI.
history: Released by Diwan Software in September 2000 and described by the company as the first digital font able to compose Quranic calligraphy with all its markings and recitation symbols, using more than three thousand glyph shapes. Diwan Mishafi won a Type Directors Club type design award in 2000.

summary: A variant of Diwan's calligraphic Mishafi Arabic font, suited to Quranic and classical texts. Ornate and formal, best at larger sizes.
history: Part of Diwan Software's Mishafi family; its file copyright runs from 1998 to 2000. Diwan introduced Mishafi in 2000 as a professional font for Quranic calligraphy, and Apple ships both Mishafi and Mishafi Gold with macOS.

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with macOS Tahoe

summary: An Armenian font family with regular, oblique, bold and bold oblique styles, paired with a serif Latin. A practical default for Armenian text on the Mac.
history: Designed by Michael Everson, a linguist and type designer known for his work encoding scripts in Unicode. It has come with Mac OS X since at least version 10.3 Panther (2003).

summary: A clean, low-contrast humanist sans for the Gurmukhi script used to write Punjabi, in seven weights with matching Latin. Good for both UI and body text.
history: Part of Ek Type's Mukta project, which aims to build one harmonious type family across Indian scripts. Mukta Mahee (the Gurmukhi member) was designed by Shuchita Grover and Noopur Datye, building on Mukta by Girish Dalvi and Yashodeep Gholap, and is released under an open license on Google Fonts.
designers: Shuchita Grover and Noopur Datye (Ek Type); base Mukta design by Girish Dalvi and Yashodeep Gholap

summary: A sturdy Arabic text font in regular, bold and black weights, paired with a Times-like Latin. Good for newspapers, books and headlines.
history: Made by Diwan Software, which says Muna became one of the most popular fonts for Arabic newspaper printing and book publishing. Its file copyright dates to 2001, and it ships with macOS.

summary: A Myanmar (Burmese) font for Burmese and other languages of Myanmar, whose Latin letters use a humanist sans with noticeable stroke contrast (the shared "MN" Latin design). Suited to reading text on the Mac.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts bundled with Apple's operating systems. It is one of the "MN" families that ship with macOS.

summary: A Myanmar (Burmese) font from Apple's "Sangam MN" series, pairing Myanmar (Burmese) letterforms with a plain grotesque-style sans serif for Latin. Good for Burmese and other languages of Myanmar text in apps and on screen.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts for Apple. The Sangam MN families are a sans-style counterpart to the MN fonts and ship with macOS.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: A simple, classic Arabic font that balances traditional shapes with easy reading. Suited to everyday Arabic text.
history: Made by Diwan Software for the Arabic Macintosh in the 1990s, designed to look good on screen and print reliably on Apple's LaserWriter. It was named after the son of the head of Apple Paris, who managed the Arabic Macintosh.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A Hebrew font family in regular, inclined, bold and bold inclined styles. A general-purpose choice for Hebrew text.
history: A Monotype Hebrew design; the font data is copyright Monotype and Type Solutions, 1990 to 1993. It was one of the Hebrew fonts in Apple's Hebrew Language Kit for classic Mac OS and still ships with macOS.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A flowing, calligraphic Nastaliq font for Urdu, where words slope diagonally down toward the baseline. The traditional look for Urdu books, poetry and signage.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, which aims to cover every script in Unicode. It was made by the Monotype Design Team and added to macOS with High Sierra (10.13).
designers: Monotype Design Team (for Google's Noto project)

summary: A simple, low-contrast sans serif font for the Batak script of Sumatra, Indonesia. Useful for displaying Batak text and learning materials.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, which aims to cover every script in Unicode, and made by the Monotype Design Team. Batak is used for the Batak languages of North Sumatra.
designers: Monotype Design Team (for Google's Noto project)

summary: A clean sans serif font for the Kannada script of Karnataka, India, in multiple weights and widths. Good for UI and body text.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, made by Jelle Bosma and the Monotype Design Team. Kannada is used to write the Kannada language and several smaller languages of South India, including Tulu and Konkani.
designers: Jelle Bosma and the Monotype Design Team

summary: A simple sans serif font for N'Ko, a right-to-left script for the Manding languages of West Africa. Useful for reading and publishing in N'Ko.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, made by the Monotype Design Team. N'Ko was devised by Solomana Kanté in 1949.
designers: Monotype Design Team (for Google's Noto project)

summary: A clean sans serif font for the Odia (Oriya) script of eastern India. Good for everyday Odia text on screen.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, which aims to cover every script in Unicode, and made by the Monotype Design Team. Odia is used mainly for the Odia language of Odisha.
designers: Monotype Design Team (for Google's Noto project)

summary: A simple sans serif font for the Sunuwar alphabet, used to write the Sunwar language of eastern Nepal and Sikkim. One of the newest scripts supported on the Mac.
history: Designed by Anshuman Pandey, originally to accompany his proposal to encode Sunuwar in Unicode, then re-engineered to meet Noto requirements. The script was added to Unicode 16.0 in 2024.

summary: A sans serif font for the right-to-left Syriac script, in the Estrangela style and nine weights. Suited to Syriac liturgical texts and modern Aramaic languages.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, made by Patrick Giasson and the Monotype Design Team. Syriac has been used to write the Syriac language since the 1st century.
designers: Patrick Giasson and the Monotype Design Team

summary: A small, simple sans serif font for Baybayin, the historical Philippine script encoded in Unicode as "Tagalog." Good for displaying Baybayin text and cultural designs.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, made by the Monotype Design Team. Baybayin was widely used in Luzon before and during the 16th and 17th centuries and has seen renewed modern interest.
designers: Monotype Design Team (for Google's Noto project)

summary: A modulated, serif-style font for the Myanmar (Burmese) script, in nine weights. Good for longer Burmese reading text.
history: Part of Google's Noto project, made by Ben Mitchell and the Monotype Design Team. The Myanmar script is used for Burmese, Mon, Shan and several other languages.
designers: Ben Mitchell and the Monotype Design Team

summary: A Odia (Oriya) font for the Odia language of eastern India, whose Latin letters use a humanist sans with noticeable stroke contrast (the shared "MN" Latin design). Suited to reading text on the Mac.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts bundled with Apple's operating systems. It is one of the "MN" families that ship with macOS.

summary: A Odia (Oriya) font from Apple's "Sangam MN" series, pairing Odia (Oriya) letterforms with a plain grotesque-style sans serif for Latin. Good for the Odia language of eastern India text in apps and on screen.
history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts for Apple. The Sangam MN families are a sans-style counterpart to the MN fonts and ship with macOS.

links.label: Fonts In Use: Sangam MN Latin

summary: Apple's clean, modern sans serif (gothic) Chinese system font, tuned for Traditional Chinese as used in Hong Kong. Ideal for UI and on-screen reading.
history: Created by DynaComware together with Apple as the Chinese system font introduced in OS X 10.11 El Capitan (2015), replacing the older STHeiti. It was designed for a modern look and crisp on-screen readability, and comes in six weights.

history: PingFang was created by DynaComware together with Apple as the Chinese system font introduced in OS X 10.11 El Capitan (2015). The MO (Macau) version is a later addition; it first appears in Apple's font list for macOS Sequoia (2024).

summary: A classical serif font for the Cherokee syllabary, with a companion Latin. Its style recalls the early metal types cut for Cherokee in the 19th century.
history: Designed by Ross Mills of Tiro Typeworks. It was also the first font Microsoft provided with Cherokee support, and it ships with both Windows and macOS.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A Hebrew font in regular and bold, paired with a Times-like serif Latin. A straightforward choice for Hebrew documents.
history: An Apple Hebrew font with a copyright of 1991 to 1995. It was one of the TrueType fonts in Apple's Hebrew Language Kit for classic Mac OS and has continued to ship with macOS.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A traditional Song (Ming) style Chinese serif font for Simplified Chinese, with thin horizontals and thick verticals. Good for printed-style body text.
history: Made by Changzhou SinoType Technology, whose "ST" fonts have long shipped with Mac OS X. In later macOS versions it is packaged together with the Songti SC fonts.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A bold, decorative Arabic font in a calligraphic style with tall strokes. Best for headings and display text rather than long reading.
history: Made by Diwan Software, which produced Arabic fonts with Apple for the Arabic Macintosh. Its file copyright dates to 2001, and it ships with macOS.

links.label: Apple: Fonts included with macOS Tahoe

summary: A Thai text font with traditional looped letterforms and a simple sans serif Latin. Suited to Thai body text.
history: One of the Thai fonts Apple has long shipped with its Mac systems, with a file copyright going back to 1992.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS
Apple: Fonts included with macOS Tahoe

summary: A Devanagari font for Hindi, Marathi, Sanskrit and other languages, with a light sans serif Latin. Its broad set of conjuncts makes it good for body text.
history: Made by Modular Infotech of Pune, India (file copyright 2000). Apple added it to the Mac with OS X 10.10 Yosemite.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A Thai font with rounded terminals, paired with a bold, blocky Latin. Works for short text and friendly headings.
history: One of the Thai fonts Apple has long shipped with its Mac systems, with a file copyright going back to 1992.

history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts for Apple. The Sangam MN families are a sans-style counterpart to the MN fonts and ship with macOS.

summary: A family of traditional Song (Ming) style Chinese serif fonts for Simplified Chinese, from light to black. Good for book-like body text and elegant headings.
history: Made by Changzhou SinoType Technology and based on its STSong design; the family's file copyright runs from 2010 to 2012. It groups SinoType's Song fonts under one name on macOS.

summary: A family of traditional Song (Ming) style Chinese serif fonts for Traditional Chinese. Good for book-like body text and formal documents.
history: Made by Changzhou SinoType Technology as the Traditional Chinese companion to Songti SC; the file copyright runs from 2010 to 2013. It ships with macOS.

links.label: Wikipedia: List of typefaces included with macOS

summary: A modern loopless Thai sans serif in six weights, designed to sit comfortably beside Latin text. Clean and good for screens, marketing and UI.
history: Designed by Anuthin Wongsunkakon of Cadson Demak for Apple (the retail version is called Sukhumvit Tadmai). It briefly became the Thai system font in the iOS 7 beta, but after pushback from Thai users Apple reverted to Thonburi; it was added to the Mac in OS X 10.10 Yosemite.

history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts bundled with Apple's operating systems. It is one of the "MN" families that ship with macOS.

history: Made by Muthu Nedumaran of the Malaysian firm Murasu Systems, which developed a series of Indic and Southeast Asian fonts bundled with Apple's operating systems. It is one of the "MN" families that ship with macOS.

summary: Apple's traditional looped Thai font, whose Latin letters match the classic Geneva. Clear on screen and a solid default for Thai text.
history: One of the Thai fonts Apple has long shipped with the Mac, with a file copyright going back to 1992. Thonburi was the Thai system font on iOS, and Apple returned to it after Thai users objected to the loopless Sukhumvit in the iOS 7 beta.

summary: A flowing, informal Arabic font modeled on everyday Ruq'a-style handwriting, in regular and light. Good for invitations, notes and personal designs.
history: Made by Diwan Software, which produced Arabic fonts with Apple for the Arabic Macintosh. Its file copyright dates to 2002, and it ships with macOS.
